title: DocumentToolbar arranges its built-in controls into three named slots, and source ships an eighth control the academy omits
content:
`DocumentToolbar` does not lay its controls out as one flat row. `defaultControlSlots` in `packages/design-system/src/connect/components/document-toolbar/constants.ts` splits them into three named groups, and `ControlSlot` is the literal union `"first" | "second" | "third"`:

```ts
export const defaultControlSlots = {
  first: ["undo", "redo", "download"],   // primary document actions
  second: ["name"],                       // document identity
  third: ["update", "history", "switchboard", "close"], // secondary actions
} as const;
```

The slot names are the addressing scheme for `customControls` — you target a group, never an index — and `documentToolbarControls` (the source of the `DocumentToolbarControlName` union that `enabledControls` / `disabledControls` accept) is derived by spreading the three slots in order, so slot membership also fixes render order.

**The eighth control.** Source has **eight** built-in controls, not seven. The `third` slot leads with `update`, mapped in `defaultControlComponents` to `ToolbarUpgradeButton`. The academy page (`00-DocumentToolbar.mdx`) lists only `["undo", "redo", "download", "name", "history", "switchboard", "close"]` and shows `third` as `["history", "switchboard", "close"]` — the doc has not been updated for the upgrade control, so treat source as authoritative here.

`ToolbarUpgradeButton` is conditional rather than always-on, which is presumably why it went unnoticed: it calls `useDocumentVersionStatus(document)` and returns `null` unless the status is `"upgrade-available"` **and** `canUpgrade` is true. When it does render, it shows an `Update available` label and its click handler fires `showPHModal({ type: "confirmDocumentUpgrade", documentId })`.

One rough edge: unlike every other built-in button, `ToolbarUpgradeButton` is **not** re-exported from the component's `index.ts`. So `update` is overridable through `componentOverrides` but the default implementation cannot be imported and wrapped the way `ToolbarDownloadButton` can.

_Source: packages/design-system/src/connect/components/document-toolbar/{constants.ts,types.ts,toolbar-button.tsx,index.ts}, cross-checked against apps/academy/docs/academy/03-Build/03-BuildingUserExperiences/06-DocumentTools/00-DocumentToolbar.mdx (Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45)._
description: Slots are first [undo, redo, download], second [name], third [update, history, switchboard, close]. The academy lists only seven controls and drops `update` from the third slot.
